risk_if_not_implemented: Without Limit Personal Data (PD) In Event Logs & Security-Relevant Telemetry, Personal Data (PD) may be collected, processed, retained or shared without lawful authority or adequate safeguards, harming individuals and exposing the organization to regulatory action. Based on the risk and threat mapping for this control, this deficiency most likely exposes the organization to Unauthorized Retention / Inability to Dispose of Data (R-AM-3), Privacy Harm / Unauthorized Processing (R-IP-6), and most likely increases susceptibility to Human Error (MT-9).

compensating_control_1.name: Centralized Collection of Event Logs & Security-Relevant Telemetry
compensating_control_1.description: Mechanisms exist to utilize a Security Incident Event Manager (SIEM), or similar automated tool, to support the centralized collection of event logs and security-relevant telemetry.
compensating_control_1.justification: Centralized Collection of Event Logs & Security-Relevant Telemetry (MON-05) provides detective monitoring capability that compensates for the absence of Limit Personal Data (PD) In Audit Records (MON-30.1) by identifying unauthorized, anomalous, or non-compliant activity that the primary control would have prevented. Given the technology-focused nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.

compensating_control_2.name: Event Log & Security-Relevant Telemetry Storage Capacity
compensating_control_2.description: Mechanisms exist to allocate and proactively manage sufficient event log and security-relevant telemetry storage capacity to reduce the likelihood of such capacity being exceeded.
compensating_control_2.justification: Event Log & Security-Relevant Telemetry Storage Capacity (MON-10) provides detective monitoring capability that compensates for the absence of Limit Personal Data (PD) In Audit Records (MON-30.1) by identifying unauthorized, anomalous, or non-compliant activity that the primary control would have prevented. Given the technology-focused nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.
